title: HTTP Status Checker
description: Write a script that takes a URL, sends a GET request, and prints the status code and a human‑readable message.
problemStatement: Create a script `http_check.py` that defines a function `check_url(url)`. It should send a GET request to the URL with a 5‑second timeout. Print the status code and a message: if 200, 'OK'; if 404, 'Not Found'; if 403, 'Forbidden'; else print the raw code. Use `raise_for_status()` only for 4xx/5xx, but catch exceptions and print 'Request failed'. Test with `'https://httpbin.org/status/200'` and `'https://httpbin.org/status/404'`.
hints: Use a dict to map codes to messages if desired.
expectedOutput:
For 200: 'Status: 200 OK'
For 404: 'Status: 404 Not Found' (or similar).
